summary: Log cabin fire lookout on the BC-US border in Manning Park, built 1930 and still standing; reached by a hiking trail of about 30 km round trip.

facts.design: Crossed-log cabin with a small glass-walled observation room on top of the main roof

staffing.status: Last used in the 1970s, per the Methow Valley association

access.note: In Manning Provincial Park and reached by a hiking trail. A hiking guide describes the trail as damaged but does not describe it as closed.

visit.trail_note: Trailhead about 3.5 km east of Gibson Pass Road, off Highway 3. Round trip about 30 km. Backcountry fees apply to overnight stays.

facts.agency: BC Parks (Ministry of Environment), per the register's source credit

events.note: Log cabin cupola constructed on the site; later surveys placed it on Canadian soil.
Canadian Register of Historic Places, entry 18048: recognized by the Province of British Columbia, date recognized December 31, 1941.
US-side 30 ft L-4 tower. The association's structure header gives 1952; its history text gives 1953.

evidence.supports: Monument 83 is a log-structure fire lookout station in a subalpine clearing at the eastern edge of E.C. Manning Park, on the border
evidence.quote: Monument 83 is a log-structure fire lookout station located in a subalpine clearing that forms the extreme east edge of E.C. Manning Park in southwestern British Columbia, at the Canada-United States border.

evidence.supports: Register praises the crossed-log wall construction
evidence.quote: as a good example of crossed-log wall construction

evidence.supports: Small glass-walled observation room on top of the main cabin roof
evidence.quote: with its small glass-walled observation room situated on top of the main cabin roof

evidence.supports: Register calls it a decommissioned lookout that shows the Forest Service's historic mandate
evidence.quote: The decommissioned lookout conveys to the public the Forest Service's historic mandate

evidence.supports: Register source credit names BC Parks
Site first established in the 1920s as a camp with tree platform
evidence.quote: was first established in the 1920s as a camp with tree platform

evidence.supports: 1930 log cabin cupola, celebrated as northernmost US lookout until found to be on Canadian soil
evidence.quote: In 1930, a log cabin cupola was constructed and celebrated as the northernmost lookout in the United States until surveys later determined it to be on Canadian soil.

evidence.supports: Structure header gives 1952 for the L4 tower
evidence.quote: Current Structure(s) Built: log cabin 1930/L4 tower 1952

evidence.supports: History text gives 1953 for the US-side L-4 tower, 30 ft
evidence.quote: In 1953 the United States built a 30′ treated timber L-4 tower

evidence.supports: Cupola on Canadian soil; L-4 tower on the US side
evidence.quote: the 1930s log cabin cupola is on Canadian soil while the 1952 L-4 tower stands on the US side

evidence.supports: Lookouts last used in the 1970s; both structures remain intact
evidence.quote: The lookouts were last used in the 1970s and both structures remain intact.

evidence.supports: Trailhead about 3.5 km east of Gibson Pass Road off Highway 3
evidence.quote: located approximately 3.5 kms east of Gibson Pass Road (Manning Park Lodge) off Crowsnest Highway 3

evidence.quote: The Monument 83 Trail has suffered significant damage from wildfires and weather events.

evidence.supports: Border re-survey placed one building in Canada
evidence.quote: a re-survey of the border placed one of the two buildings within Canada.
Backcountry fees apply if staying overnight.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The association's page gives 1952 in its structure header and 1953 in its history text. The story reports both years and does not choose one.

sources.title: Monument 83
sources.publisher: Heritage Guide (text of Canadian Register of Historic Places entry 18048)

notes_for_editor: The historicplaces.ca register page did not render in the cache (only its title), so the register text is cited through the Heritage Guide mirror, which reproduces it word for word. The Methow Valley page is undated, so 'remain intact' is as of an unknown date. The Rainlander guide is dated to 2026 in its introduction, but its Monument 83 trail notes carry no date of their own; check current trail status with BC Parks before publishing. The brief's kind 'ground' is not a field here and was not changed; the site is a cabin with an observation room, with a US-side tower in addition. The US tower year is left as both 1952 and 1953.
